findings.title: Default ingest endpoint sends session artifacts and bearer token over plaintext HTTP
findings.what: The default endpoint is `http://probaitio-dashboard.probaitio-system.svc`. The related baseline shipper passes the ingest bearer token in the Authorization header and uploads selected ~/.claude session-data artifacts to this URL, so any workload or network observer able to intercept in-cluster traffic can recover both sensitive session content and the reusable credential.
findings.fix: Terminate TLS at the dashboard ingest Service and change the default to an `https://` service URL, with the shipper configured to trust the issuing CA. Do not silently fall back to HTTP.
findings.acceptance: Render the default manager deployment and verify PROBAITIO_INGEST_URL begins with `https://`; then perform an ingest through the in-cluster Service using the configured CA and verify a plaintext HTTP listener cannot accept the bearer-authenticated artifact request.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read line 18 at baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba and traced only the directly related baseline path: the manager propagates this value to the artifact-ship sidecar, which reads ~/.claude session-data, constructs an artifact body, and sends it with `Authorization: Bearer <PROBAITIO_INGEST_TOKEN>` using native fetch. The literal HTTP scheme therefore governs both payload and credential transport; this is not a comment-only, speculative, or stale claim.
